original_card.question: Does a new paid-profile or mixture-ceiling claim have independent source-bound coverage of its actual changed ledger?
methods: Independently reconstruct one changed paid ledger or pooled dual with exact source and model binding.
Check a genuinely uncovered moment implication with a different enclosure method and semantic controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Choose one uncovered implication in #4088 literal mixed fill, #4091 pooled dual/model binding or #4067 changed frame/host bill. #4091 pins an earlier #4088 head: validate word, capacity and stock equivalence before applying that ceiling to the later fill.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Independently reconstruct one changed ledger or pooled certificate with a positive case and a semantic failure control. Compare exact sources and name what existing checks miss. Keep this separate from supplier-boundary-audit (ordinary/outer dispatch) and uniform-transfer-audit (all-size proof). Stop after the chosen implication; more digits of an unchanged root are not additional mechanism coverage.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.

actual_scope: Compare the byte-level THREE/FOUR words, template capacities and stock coefficient of staged-fourth-mixture-ceiling with staged544-mixed-fourth-entry, and place the recorded 1090-call root against the pooled ceiling and the 1080-call literal root.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a mixture-ceiling claim has independent source-bound coverage of its changed ledger. Its first step names this comparison: #4091 pins an earlier #4088 head, so word, capacity and stock equivalence have to be checked before that ceiling is applied to the later 1090-call fill. This package does that comparison. It does not search residual exchanges or rerun four-provider admission.
bottleneck_link: The selected frontier stays at 60403/20000000. A higher conditional endpoint still has to pass the pooled two-word invoice. Equivalence shows that the #4091 ceiling remains a valid cap for the later fill's words, capacities and stock, while the 1.951e-9 headroom of the 1080-call literal is a different gap from the 1090-call root.
stop_rule: Stop after the word, capacity and stock identities, the two exact root separations, and the three failure controls. Do not replay the 841-pattern linear program, the native stages, or the ordinary/outer release.
evidence: python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/staged-fourth-ceiling-equivalence. The four word gzip files and the owner template and order are byte-identical. Both rebuilt profiles have paid mass 65088*360. The 1090-call root sits strictly above the 1080 literal upper by 810594906779329/10^24 and strictly below the pooled ceiling lower by 1140318244487201/10^24. Three semantic controls reject a shifted profile, the 1080 idle on the 1090 selector, and a truncated word.
